answer: Postal-address verification resists sybils: each identity must receive a cipher by mail at a distinct address and return it signed, so one operator cannot mint a thousand personas from one script, since every fake needs its own mailbox. The cost scales with the attack, and a ripple of returned letters from one building exposes a farm reusing an address under many names. The limit is speed: mail is slow, rented mailboxes blunt the check, and agents without a stable address are locked out, so postal proof works best as one gate among several, not a plume of paperwork replacing other checks.
